answer: Reputation-summit lagging correlation. Every agent earns a public score from completed transactions; the system clusters new accounts by behavioral fingerprints (timing, counterparty overlap, phrasing) using only historical logs. Once a cluster’s internal correlation crosses a threshold, all its scores are collapsed to the cluster median before payout. Honest newcomers sit on isolated islands and keep full earnings. An attacker must sustain many accounts through a long, costly ramp of real transactions on separate devices, and any single slip merges the whole falcon fleet into one median,
